Intensities of Emission Lines on a Curve of Growth

Source: R/curve_of_growth.R
curve_of_growth_model.Rd

Computes the integrated intensities and optical depths of emission lines of a homogeneous plasma in LTE, given the column density of their species, by the model of curve_of_growth(), for simulations and for checking a fit.

Usage

curve_of_growth_model(
  lines,
  temperature,
  scale,
  optical_depth,
  units = "energy"
)

Arguments

lines

A data frame with one row per line and columns species (such as "K I"), intensity (integrated intensity, corrected for the spectral response), wavelength (nm), Aki (s\(^{-1}\)), gk, Ek and Ei (upper and lower level energies, eV) and stark_width (the Stark full width at half maximum, nm).

temperature

The plasma temperature, in K.

scale

The factor \(F\) of the instrument and geometry.

optical_depth

The largest optical depth at the line center of the lines of each species, which sets its column density: one value, or one per species named by species.

units

The units of intensity: "energy" (default) or "photons", as in boltzmann().

Value

A tibble with, for each line, its wavelength, optical_depth, self-absorption coefficient SA, intensity and the intensity of an optically thin plasma (thin_intensity).

See also

curve_of_growth()

Examples

lines <- data.frame(species = "Ca I", wavelength = c(400, 520), Aki = c(1.5e8, 3e7),
                    gk = c(4, 6), Ei = c(0, 2), stark_width = 0.02)
lines$Ek <- lines$Ei + 1239.842 / lines$wavelength
curve_of_growth_model(lines, temperature = 9000, scale = 1, optical_depth = 5)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   wavelength optical_depth    SA intensity thin_intensity
#>        <dbl>         <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1        400         5     0.472  1.40e-16       2.96e-16
#> 2        520         0.310 0.927  1.21e-17       1.30e-17
